title: Stockholders' Equity Fundamentals
description: Understand the major components of stockholders' equity and how transactions affect them.
html:
What is stockholders' equity?

Stockholders' equity represents the residual interest in a corporation's assets after deducting its liabilities.

Assets − Liabilities = Stockholders' Equity

Major components

  • Common Stock
  • Preferred Stock, when applicable
  • Additional Paid-In Capital
  • Retained Earnings
  • Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income or Loss
  • Treasury Stock

Contributed capital

Contributed capital generally represents amounts invested by shareholders in exchange for shares.

Retained earnings

Retained earnings generally represents accumulated earnings of the corporation that have not been distributed to shareholders as dividends.

Simple retained earnings example

Beginning Retained Earnings = $100,000

Net Income = $30,000

Dividends = $8,000

Ending Retained Earnings = $100,000 + $30,000 − $8,000 = $122,000

Treasury stock

Treasury stock consists of a corporation's own shares that were issued and later reacquired.

Treasury stock is generally presented as a reduction of stockholders' equity rather than as an asset.

Remember

Assets − Liabilities = Equity

Net income generally increases retained earnings.

Dividends generally reduce retained earnings.

Treasury stock generally reduces total stockholders' equity.

quiz.prompt: Beginning retained earnings is $80,000, net income is $25,000 and dividends are $10,000. What is ending retained earnings?
